mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate compresses discount rates applied to equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of economic conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate exceeding 0.5 percentage points over three months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rises by more than 0.5pp over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales indicate broad-based consumer demand contraction, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline by more than 1% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 220), the Federal Reserve's tightening response produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 220.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production exceeding 1% over one month signals imminent economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO falls by more than 1% in one month.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of industrial production indicates robust economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of economic conditions.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window for INDPRO as a predictor of 20-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: In strong labor market growth regimes (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly), sustained consumer spending drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in inflation and federal funds rate signal aggressive monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS increase by more than 0.5% and 0.1% respectively in one month.
